deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is the first page of an official cover letter on printed Institut de France / Académie des Sciences letterhead (helmeted head vignette), dated Paris, 24 March 1875 (the last digit of the year is written in an unusual form, but 1875 is consistent with the context). It is from the Secrétaire perpétuel of the Académie des Sciences. It is addressed to Professor (Friedrich) Wöhler in Göttingen, foreign associate (associé étranger) of the Académie.

Content of this page: in response to Wöhler's letter of the 3rd of that month, the Secretary sends under cover the original of the memoir Riemann submitted to the Académie's prize competition (concours). The letter dates that competition to 1861; in fact the question was set in 1858 and the closing date was 1861. Its subject is quoted only by its opening: 'Trouver quel doit être l'état calorifique d'un corps solide homogène indéfini etc.' The page breaks off at 'Les règlements de l'Académie s'opposent, Monsieur,'.

The next page completes the thought:
- The Académie's rules forbid such communications, but the aim pursued by Professor Weber is too praiseworthy to refuse help.
- The Académie trusts Wöhler's discretion.
- The manuscript must be returned to the Archives once printing is finished.
- The letter is signed 'Pour le Secrétaire perpétuel et par autorisation', apparently by (Ernest) Maindron of the secretariat.

Historical context (my addition): the memoir is Riemann's 'Commentatio mathematica, qua respondere tentatur quaestioni ab Ill.ma Academia Parisiensi propositae' (1861). In it Riemann treats the conditions under which an anisotropic heat-conduction problem can be reduced to the isotropic one. This leads to the invariants of a quadratic differential form, the Riemann curvature tensor and flatness criteria. The prize was never awarded, partly because Riemann's proofs were incomplete; the question was withdrawn in 1868. The loan of the original manuscript was evidently arranged so that Heinrich Weber (with Dedekind) could print the Commentatio in Riemann's Gesammelte mathematische Werke (1876). The bundle 'R.Waermeleitung' thus begins with this administrative document recording the provenance and loan of the manuscript.
errors: Minor historical imprecision in the letter itself: the competition question was set in 1858; 1861 was the closing date and the year Riemann submitted his memoir. Calling it the 'concours ouvert en 1861' is loose but not seriously wrong.

results.what: Archival/administrative record: the Paris Académie loaned Riemann's original 1861 prize memoir (the Commentatio on heat conduction) to Wöhler in Göttingen in March 1875, at Weber's request, for its publication in Riemann's collected works.
results.modern_name: Provenance of Riemann's 'Commentatio mathematica' (Paris prize memoir, 1861)
results.usually_credited_to: Known from the editorial notes to Riemann's Gesammelte Werke (1876, ed. H. Weber with R. Dedekind)

deep.surprise_reason: This is an administrative cover letter from the Académie des Sciences, not mathematics by Riemann. It documents the well-known circumstance that Weber obtained the Paris prize memoir for the 1876 edition of Riemann's works. It is of mild archival interest but contains no new mathematical content.
transcription_corrections: Addressee is written 'Wohler' (without the umlaut) in the manuscript; the person is Friedrich Wöhler.
'associé Etranger' should be 'Associé Etranger' (capital A, as in the image).
The year in the date line is written '187' plus an unusual final glyph; '1875' is the plausible reading and fits the context (Gesammelte Werke 1876).
A pencil folio number '83' appears in the right margin, not included in the transcription.
The salutation reads 'Monsieur & Très Honoré Confrère' as transcribed, with 'Monsieur' in an abbreviated or cursive form.
The rest of the transcription agrees with the image.
